architecture.mechanism: Engineered micro-nondecorated surface topography combined with intrinsic hydrophobicity physically inhibits sessile organism settlement while entrapped gas pockets in microstructures generate a slip boundary condition that reduces near-wall turbulence intensity and wall shear stress.
architecture.intervention: Apply a thin conformal overlay of micro-patterned PDMS containing micro-cylinder textures sized to barnacle cyprid larvae dimensions directly over the existing conventional antifouling paint using an underwater-compatible adhesive or spray-on method during the scheduled dry-dock window 18 months out, without stripping or modifying the coating system of record.
architecture.expected_effect: Partial reduction in larval and juvenile fouling onset rate and measurable decrease in skin-friction drag from the slip-effect, offsetting a portion of the 12–18% fuel consumption penalty and partially recovering lost service speed between dry-docking cycles.
architecture.falsification_test: Deploy a 5 m² instrumented panel coated with the micro-patterned PDMS overlay on the hull mid-section; after a 90-day sea trial measure both settlement coverage percentage versus an uncoated reference panel and shaft power required to maintain constant speed — if settlement reduction is below 30% or drag reduction is negligible, the mechanism does not transfer effectively at full-scale Reynolds numbers.
